input.question: Why didn't we actively re-center the ranges to follow the price (frequent narrowing), instead of staying wide?
input.reference: On 720 days 0 of 21 narrow configurations passed the gate, and the one live narrowing (31.08 to 11.09) ended -$32 vs HODL, so on 16.09 narrowing was rejected again because the upside (about +$1 per episode) is far smaller than the loss when the price leaves a ±5% range (about -$30).
input.answer: The project rejected frequent re-centering because 720-day backtests showed it lost to passive wide ranges even in flat regimes. The mechanism was that while narrowing earned ~4× more fees, the implied loss (IL) from re-centering realized the divergence, eroding ~$1.9k–$2.9k more than the fee gains. The team concluded that a narrow range acts like a short gamma position, where every posture change realizes a loss. The initial belief that IL was negligible in flat markets was proven false, and the strategy ultimately remained wide passive LP.

Zwężanie przegrywa nawet tam, gdzie miało wygrywać.

input.question: Why did the LP earn less in fees during an uptrend than in a flat market?
input.reference: Fees accrue only while the price is inside the range and fee yield scales roughly with 1/width, so a narrow range earns much more in a flat market but is left behind in a trend, while a wide range stays in range but earns several times less; the journal states this mechanism (the basis of FlatWide) but has no live measurement of fees during an uptrend, and it attributes the backtest losses in up windows to impermanent loss and LVR rather than to lower fees.
input.answer: In an uptrend the LP earns fewer fees than in a flat market because a narrow range is out of position as the price rises. The journal explains this as “short gamma”: “Wąskie pasmo to short gamma: każde przejście postury REALIZUJE dywergencję” (a narrow band is short gamma; every posture change realizes divergence). Consequently, in UP windows the LP posts losses while in FLAT windows it wins: “We FLAT wszystko wygrywa” but “W UP … W DOWN: 20-42%wygr, wszystkie średnie ujemne.” The 720d breakdown confirms it: “up 0% wygranych, śr. −13.91,” whereas “flat 72%, +0.53.” The fee itself is not the problem—the narrow LP actually earned more fee in flat periods—but in a trend the price leaves the range, so the LP stops collecting and realizes losses on rebalancing, whereas a flat market keeps the position in range and fee-earning.

We FLAT wszystko wygrywa
up 0% wygranych, śr. −13.91

input.question: What does the function fetchFreshPool do?
input.reference: It re-reads the pool state on-chain (factory.getPool, then slot0 and liquidity) right before the mint step of a rebalance or rotation, so the new position is built from the current price instead of the price captured when the modal opened, and falls back to the old pool if the lookup fails; it was added after the 11.09 widening failed once on 'Price slippage check' and was never exercised live, since the only later chance (a FLAT_NARROW card on 16.09) was not signed and the positions were closed by hand in Uniswap.
input.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) fetches the latest pool state by calling factory.getPool, reading slot0 and liquidity, and constructing a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It uses a fail-open strategy: if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the stale pool object instead of throwing. It is invoked in useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution immediately before buildMintStep to ensure up-to-date price data for mint calculations.
